history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Presbyterian church in Bairabi, Kolasib district, Mizoram, under the Presbyterian Church of India (Mizoram Synod). Per 2011 census data, Bairabi's population is ~87.7% Christian, and local directories list the Presbyterian Church of India among Bairabi's churches. Identity caveat: map listings show several Presbyterian congregations around Bairabi (Bairabi Presbyterian Church, Bairabi Dinthar Presbyterian Church, Bairabi Railway Station Presbyterian Church), so the generic name 'Bairabi Presbyterian Church' is ambiguous; coordinates used are those published for the 'Bairabi Presbyterian Church' place listing and should be treated as approximate. In December 2024 the Mizoram Presbyterian Church Synod approved the creation of a new Bairabi Presbytery (comprising Hmarthlang, Kolasib and Teirei Presbyteries). CSV state column was wrong (held the town name); actual state is Mizoram. No overlap with an existing dataset file; id differs from 2464.json (Dhirdham Temple, Darjeeling).

town_description: Bairabi is a border town in Kolasib district, Mizoram, on the Assam frontier. It is a trade and transport hub with a thermal power station, the Bairabi railway terminus on the Bairabi-Sairang line, and a mixed Christian-Hindu-Muslim population (2011 census: Christian 87.73%, Hindu 2.85%, Muslim 8.77%).
